This homework applies the **multivariate Bayesian regression workflow** from Week 9 to a new substantive question.

**The research question**: *Is education associated with higher income, after accounting for gender?*

**The dataset**: `data/income_education.csv` contains 250 synthetic individual observations.
The variables are:

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `person_id` | Unique person identifier (P001–P250) |
| `gender` | Gender (0 = man, 1 = woman) |
| `education` | Years of schooling |
| `income` | Annual income in thousands of EUR — the **outcome variable** |

Work through the sections in order.
Your rendered PDF should contain all code, plots, and written answers.

# Pre-Model {#sec-pre}

## Data Exploration {#sec-explore}

Compute numerical summaries and produce exploratory plots for all variables in the dataset.

## DAG {#sec-dag}

Draw a directed acyclic graph (DAG) representing your assumed data-generating process for this research question.

## Estimand {#sec-estimand}

State in plain language the quantity you want to learn from the data, and explain whether this estimand is descriptive or causal.

# Model {#sec-model}

## Formal Model Specification {#sec-model-spec}

Write the full statistical model in mathematical notation, specifying the likelihood and the linear predictor.

## Prior Specification {#sec-priors}

Choose priors for all model parameters and justify each choice on principled grounds.

## Prior Predictive Check {#sec-prior-check}

Simulate predicted outcomes from the prior distribution alone and assess whether the implied outcomes fall in a plausible range.

## Model Fitting {#sec-fit}

Fit the model using `brms` with four chains and explicit `prior =` arguments.

# Post-Model {#sec-post}

## Convergence Assessment {#sec-convergence}

Check that the sampler converged by examining $\hat{R}$, effective sample size, and traceplots for all parameters.

## Posterior Predictive Check {#sec-ppc}

Assess whether the fitted model reproduces the observed income distribution.

## Interpretation {#sec-interpretation}

Summarize the posterior distributions of the key parameters and visualize the partial effect of education on income.

## Discussion {#sec-discussion}

Write 2–3 sentences reporting the substantive finding in plain, non-technical language.
